authors: Iizuka, R., Xia, J. & Yokoya, N.
title: Frequency-based optimal style mix for domain generalization in semantic segmentation of remote sensing images
source: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing 62, 1-14
relevance: The remote-sensing-specific realization of everything Search 24/26/28 converged on: mix STYLE in the frequency domain, but keep the frequencies that carry segmentation signal and randomize only the rest (its 'optimal mix'), plus a consistency regularizer. That refinement matters for us because a blunt amplitude swap (FDA, ID 136) risks destroying the fine texture that distinguishes a crown from a lawn at 7.5 cm - FOSMix explicitly preserves the essential frequencies instead. Peer-reviewed in TGRS, code public, and it names location, TIME and SENSOR as the shifts it targets, which is our exact triple.

authors: Rafi, T.H., Mahjabin, R., Ghosh, E., Ko, Y.-W. & Lee, J.-G.
title: Domain generalization for semantic segmentation: a survey
relevance: Peer-reviewed survey of the field our problem actually belongs to, organizing methods into augmentation/randomization, feature normalization and disentanglement, and meta-learning families. Gives us the map we lacked for the first sixteen iterations, when we were searching domain ADAPTATION vocabulary and finding the wrong shelf. Use it to check the loop's coverage for whole families we have missed, rather than continuing to sample the literature one method at a time.
